# Annotator contract template

The full contract is still in draft. The clause below can be used now.

## Review, rejection and appeal

*Fill in the bracketed fields. This clause sets out how submitted work is reviewed and how an annotator can contest a rejection. The practice behind it is described in [Review submitted work](../3_annotation-design/workflow-adjudication.md#review-submitted-work).*

**In plain language:** someone other than you checks your work. They can accept it, correct it, or reject it. If they reject it, they must tell you why. If you think the rejection is wrong, you can ask once for it to be looked at again, and you will always be told the result.

1. **Review.** Submitted work is reviewed by a person other than the annotator, against the annotation guideline and reviewer rubric in force at the time, version [VERSION].
2. **Verdicts.** Each reviewed item is accepted, corrected and accepted, or rejected. Corrected work counts as accepted work by the annotator, and the annotator can see what was changed.
3. **Reasons.** Every rejection comes with a written reason that the annotator can see.
4. **Revision.** Rejected work is returned to the annotator, who may revise and resubmit it within [TIME PERIOD].
5. **Re-review.** An annotator who believes a rejection is wrong may request one re-review of that verdict, with a written reason, within [TIME PERIOD] of being told. Where possible, a different reviewer handles it. The annotator is told the outcome in every case.
6. **Outcome.** A rejection upheld on re-review is final. A rejection overturned on re-review is recorded as accepted. A resubmitted item that is rejected again receives a new verdict, which can be contested once in the same way; after [N] rounds of revision the item is closed and its final verdict is recorded.
7. **Feedback timing.** Annotators receive their verdicts [CADENCE, for example at the end of each review session].
8. **Records.** Verdicts, reasons, re-review requests and their outcomes are recorded and kept for [RETENTION PERIOD]. An annotator may ask to see the records about their own work by contacting [CONTACT].
